sections.h2: What is the Green, Ohio housing market like?
sections.html:
Green is a suburban city in southeastern Summit County between Akron and Canton, and it is large by area: about 32 square miles of land, with 1.5 square miles of water. That makes for a spread-out market of subdivisions, lakeside lots and former farm parcels rather than a compact grid.

Green Township was created in 1809 as part of Stark County and joined Summit County when that county formed in 1840. Hamlets such as Greensburg dotted the township, farms gave way to developers after 1950, and voters approved merging the village with the rest of the township in 1991. The city's motto, "A township from the past, a city of the future," reflects that history.

The market served by this page covers the city's ZIP codes 44232, 44312, 44319, 44685 and 44216, so a house with a Green address may sit near neighboring cities. Confirm that your parcel is inside the city limits before relying on city rules.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about homes in Green?
sections.html:
Green's numbers show a settled, owner-heavy suburb. Three in four households own, and the typical owned home is valued at $280,200, while the median household income is $95,047.

The 2020 Census counted 27,475 residents, with a median age of 43.1, which is above the national profile. Of 11,825 housing units, 5.3 percent were vacant. Many Green owners have lived in their homes for a long time: 89.7 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

sections.h2: What are the zoning and code rules in Green?
sections.html:
The city's Zoning Division issues permits, inspects new structures and enforces the City Code, and it also takes right-of-way applications for aprons and road openings. Its Zoning page lists the most common code complaints:

  • High grass
  • Litter, garbage and debris
  • Junk or inoperable vehicles
  • Storage of RVs, campers and boats
  • Property disrepair

Clearing these before listing avoids a surprise from a buyer's walkthrough. The division is at the Central Administration Building, 1755 Town Park Blvd., and its phone is 330-896-6605. The Land Development Code is in Part Twelve of the city's codified ordinances.

Building permits for structures run through Summit County. The city's page points to the Summit County Department of Building Standards in Akron and to Summit County Public Health, which is at 1867 West Market Street, Akron, phone 330-926-5600, for septic and well questions.

sections.h2: What does the Summit County Fiscal Office charge to transfer a Green deed?
sections.html:
The Fiscal Office's fee page lists a conveyance fee of $4.00 per $1,000, rounded up to the next $100 of the sale price, and a lot fee of 50 cents per lot named in the legal description, which applies to exempt and non-exempt transfers alike. Summit's rate is higher than the $3 per $1,000 charged in some neighboring counties.

Per the Property Transfer page, the department accepts the DTE 100 statement of value or the DTE 100(EX) exemption form, under ORC 319.202 and 319.54(G)(3). Properly prepared forms must reach the Property Transfer Department by 3:30 p.m. to have the legal description approved the same business day.

Recording takes place at the Fiscal Office's Recording Division, 175 South Main Street, 4th floor, Akron. Ohio law (ORC 5301.25) requires a deed to be recorded in the county where the land lies, and an unrecorded deed is treated as fraudulent against a later buyer without notice. Ask the Recording Division for the current page charge, because the fee page and the state schedule changed in recent years.

sections.h2: Which employers and amenities draw buyers to Green?
sections.html:
Green sits at the edge of two metro areas, and its job base reflects that. The 2022 annual financial report, as quoted on Wikipedia, lists Green Local School District as the largest employer with 632 jobs, followed by:

  • Summa Health System, 555
  • Fannie May Confection, 550
  • FedEx Custom Critical, 495
  • Diebold Nixdorf, 427
  • Target, 369

Interstate 77 serves the city, and the Akron-Canton Regional Airport lies partly inside Green and partly in Jackson Township. Green built the first two-lane roundabout in Summit County in 2009 and had 11 roundabouts as of 2024, so buyers from elsewhere notice the traffic pattern.

Boettler Park, a 26-acre park with trails, fishing and picnic areas, and the Singer Lake Bog nature preserve are two public spaces often mentioned alongside Green. Public school students attend Green Local Schools.

sections.h2: What should a Green seller know about pipelines and local history?
sections.html:
Green fought the NEXUS Pipeline in court starting in 2016 because the line runs near residential neighborhoods, wetlands and the Comet Lake Dam. Construction began in 2018 after the city reached a $7.5 million settlement. If your lot is near the route, a buyer may ask where the easement sits, and you can confirm that on your title paperwork.

Land use changed quickly after 1950 as farmers sold to developers, so Green houses range from older farmhouses to newer subdivision homes. The Levi J. Hartong Farmhouse, pictured on the city's Wikipedia page, is one of the older structures.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a Green house quickly?
sections.html:
• Agent listing: best for move-in-ready homes in subdivisions with comparable recent sales.
  • Investor sale: suited to dated farmhouses, houses with code violations, or an estate sale.
  • Owner sale: saves commission but requires you to prepare the DTE 100 and deed paperwork.

Whichever route you pick, price the house against nearby Green sales, check for open zoning complaints, and gather the survey, title and any septic records.

faqs.q: Who handles building permits for a Green house?
faqs.a: The City of Green Zoning Division issues zoning permits and does inspections of new structures, while the Summit County Department of Building Standards and Summit County Public Health handle county and state level building and health matters.

faqs.q: What does Summit County charge to transfer a Green deed?
faqs.a: The Fiscal Office lists $4.00 per $1,000 of sale price, rounded up to the next $100, plus 50 cents per lot. Forms received by 3:30 p.m. can be approved the same day.

faqs.q: Where is a Green deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Summit County Fiscal Office Recording Division, 175 South Main Street, 4th floor, Akron. Ohio law has deeds recorded in the county where the land lies.

faqs.q: Is Green a good fit for older buyers?
faqs.a: Census figures show 20.9 percent of residents are 65 or older and a median age of 43.1, so many Green homes are sold by long-time owners. Listings that highlight one-floor living can suit that group.

faqs.q: Does Green have a rental registry or point-of-sale inspection?
faqs.a: The Zoning Division's page lists code enforcement and permits, and no point-of-sale inspection program. If you plan to rent the house out instead of selling, ask the Zoning Division at 330-896-6605 about city rules first.
